title: How vizexplainer works
subtitle: A toolkit that lets AI agents turn their understanding of a codebase into a polished, interactive page.
summary: An agent studies some code, drafts an explanation one chapter at a time, and vizexplainer combines the chapters into a single HTML file anyone can open. This page explains the toolkit's own source code.

agent.label: AI agent
agent.summary: Reads the codebase, decides what to explain and in which order, and writes the explainer document.

reader.label: Reader
reader.summary: Anyone with a browser: a developer, a manager, a student. No install needed.

doc.label: explainer.json
doc.summary: The manifest: shared entities and relations, metadata, and an ordered list of chapter JSON files.

output.label: explainer.html
output.summary: One self-contained file with all CSS, scripts, diagrams and highlighted code inlined. Works offline and on any static host.

src.label: src
src.summary: All of the toolkit's TypeScript source.

build.label: build.ts
build.summary: Orchestrates loading, component setup, rendering and page assembly.

issues.label: issues.ts
issues.summary: Problems are collected with exact paths like `blocks[2].children[0]` plus *did you mean* hints, so an agent can fix them without guessing.

html.label: html.ts
html.summary: A tiny safe templating helper: interpolated values are escaped unless they are already HTML.

document.label: document
document.summary: The data model: what an explainer *is*, independent of how it looks.

schema.label: schema.ts
schema.summary: Zod schemas for documents, entities, relations, sources and blocks.

model.label: model.ts
model.summary: An indexed, read-only view of entities and relations, plus cross-reference checks the schema can't express.

define.label: define.ts
define.summary: The component contract: a name, a description for agents, a props schema and a render function.

registry.label: registry.ts
registry.summary: Combines built-in components with the document's custom ones and checks each custom module's shape.

builtin.label: builtin/
builtin.summary: Twenty ready-made components, from sections and prose to graphs, sequence and state diagrams, diffs and quizzes.

render.label: render
render.summary: Turns a validated document into HTML.

engine.label: engine.ts
engine.summary: Walks the block tree, validates each block against its component, and gives components a render context.

code.label: code.ts
code.summary: Reads source files, slices line ranges and highlights them with Shiki at build time.

markdown.label: markdown.ts
markdown.summary: Markdown with one addition: `[[entity-id]]` becomes an interactive reference.

panels.label: entity-panels.ts
panels.summary: Pre-renders a details panel for every entity: summary, source and connections.

page.label: page.ts
page.summary: The page shell: top bar, table of contents, hero, detail panel, and the CSS and scripts of only the components actually used.

assets.label: assets
assets.summary: Plain CSS and JavaScript inlined into every page.

theme.label: theme.css
theme.summary: Design tokens (colours, type, radii) with automatic light and dark mode. Custom components reuse them.

runtime.label: runtime.js
runtime.summary: Browser behaviour shared by all components: linked highlighting, the details panel, focus spotlighting and the table of contents.

elk.label: ELK
elk.summary: Eclipse Layout Kernel, used to lay out graphs at build time so pages ship plain SVG.

shiki.label: Shiki
shiki.summary: The syntax highlighter used by VS Code's themes; runs at build time.

zod.label: Zod
zod.summary: Schema validation; also produces the JSON Schema agents can read.
